item: R173 follow-up: a temp file left by a killed trim is swept by the next trim; the rows' bytes and the lock leftovers are pinned
summary: The unique trim temp name (f.tmp.PID) would pile up if launchers were killed between tail and mv, so the next trim removes any f.tmp.N whose launcher pid is dead (bash and PowerShell) and keeps a live one's. Measured and pinned: every row of the three evidence files has the exact bytes it had before the lock (shape test, time and pids blanked); after a normal exit the flock path leaves three EMPTY .lock files (0 bytes) in diagnostics and the mkdir path leaves nothing; a holder killed with SIGKILL leaves its lock directory (a pid file of at most 8 bytes) which the next append takes over and removes; and the filter is handed the helper source to eval (no exported function, pinned by source and by a run under the one-true-awk).
